verdict.rationale: Conductor's docs describe cloud workspaces as sandboxes that spin up in seconds, where agents keep working after you close your laptop. The agent can run builds and setup without per-step confirmation, and the API lets you create cloud workspaces and send prompts programmatically, so background delegation to an isolated cloud environment is a first-party capability. The community comment that Conductor uses local worktrees describes the earlier local mode and does not show the cloud feature failing. Missing for 10: detailed documentation of the cloud sandbox's isolation guarantees, and independent or hands-on corroboration of long-running cloud background execution.

support.subject: As a developer, I can delegate longer-running coding tasks to run in the background in an isolated cloud environment

citations.quote: Sandboxes spin up in seconds, and agents keep working after you close your laptop.
The agent can test your repositories, update install and setup scripts, and run builds — without asking you to confirm each step.
Create workspaces, send prompts to the coding agent, and read its replies.
PR comments and failing-check logs now load while a cloud workspace is asleep.
